samples.summary: The per-editor apply loop is copy-pasted three times. `planListLevelChanges()` is correctly shared, but the write half (`applyListLevelChanges`: iterate plan → `setBlockType(id,'list-item',{listKind,listLevel})`) is duplicated verbatim in `editor.ts` (~1592), `text-box-editor.ts` (~810) and `text-editor.ts` (~2711). Only `editor.ts` adds the extra `markDirty` step, so the other two are byte-identical bodies with identical doc comments. This is inside-the-codebase tidiness (behavior is as specified), but it is the same class of triplication the issue set out to remove and will drift the next time the write step changes (e.g. if the other editors also need dirty-marking).

Unrequested scope folded in: `text-editor.ts`'s multi-block walker branch was switched from `this.doc.document.blocks[i]` to `getContextBlocks()[i]`. That fixes a distinct pre-existing bug (header/footer multi-block selections resolving indices against the body array), which affects the non-list `marginLeft ± 36` path too, not just list levels. It is adjacent and defensible, but it is not in the issue's plan or its Out-of-scope list, and the design-doc section added in `docs/design/docs/docs.md` records only the subtree rule — nothing about context-relative index resolution, so the reason this branch must read the active context is captured only in a code comment.

The planner groups selected blocks by *array object identity* (`Map<ReadonlyArray<Block>, Set<string>>`), so correctness of the list-context split depends on every walker handing back the same live array instance for one container. It happens to hold today (`getContextBlocks()` returns the live `_document.blocks`/`header.blocks`, cells return `cell.blocks`), but the fallbacks already break it: `siblingsOf` returns a fresh `[block]` when the cell lookup misses, and `getContextBlocks()` returns a fresh `[]` when no header exists. A container key (context id / table+row+col) would express the intent the design doc states ("separate list contexts") without relying on reference identity.

Design-doc arithmetic is off: the new section says "All six writers route through it" and then enumerates seven handlers (`handleTab`, `handleIndent`, `handleOutdent` in text-editor.ts, plus `indent`/`outdent` in both editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts). The task doc phrases it as "four entry points (6 handlers)"; the design doc's count matches neither.

`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is now the canonical ceiling in `packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts` and clipboard.ts was correctly switched to it, but `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:85` still hardcodes `Math.min(8, n)` for the same ceiling (slides already depends on docs). Pre-existing and out of this issue's scope, but it is the one remaining copy of the constant this change set out to centralize.
searchedFor: grep listLevel in packages/notes/src and packages/board/src

finding.summary: Header/footer fix is only applied to the caret-only branch of `forEachBlockInSelection`; the top-level multi-block branch still walks `doc.document.blocks` while indexing with the context-aware `doc.getBlockIndex()`
finding.evidence: The delta changes `siblingsOf()` (text-editor.ts:2865) to `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` precisely because "the caret can sit in a header/footer list, whose blocks live outside the body array". But the sibling walker's multi-block branch still does `const startIdx = this.doc.getBlockIndex(range.anchor.blockId)` (2831) / `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` (2836) and then `fn(topLevel[i], topLevel)`. `Doc.getBlockIndex` resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:271-273), so with a multi-block selection inside a header/footer the indices are header-relative but the array is the body — Tab/Cmd+] plans levels for the wrong blocks (or dereferences `undefined` when the header has more blocks than the body), i.e. the header-list outcome this delta claims is unmet for selections and can mis-mutate body content. Note editor.ts's sibling walker (editor.ts:1689) already uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` here, so the two parallel implementations of the same walker now disagree.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the multi-block branch of TextEditor.forEachBlockInSelection still walks `this.doc.document.blocks` (quoted as text-editor.ts:2836, `const topLevel = ...`, `fn(topLevel[i], topLevel)`). It does not. At text-editor.ts:2843 the branch resolves `const contextBlocks = this.doc.getContextBlocks();` and iterates `contextBlocks[i]`, calling `fn(b, contextBlocks)` (2845-2856), so the array matches the context-aware indices from `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)` (2831-2832, resolving via document.ts:271-273). The lines 2836-2842 the finding quotes as the defect are actually a comment explaining why `getContextBlocks()` is used instead of `document.blocks` for exactly the header/footer case. Grep confirms no `topLevel` identifier exists anywhere in text-editor.ts, and the other `doc.document.blocks` uses (e.g. 2669 in handlePageBreak) are unrelated. The claimed divergence from editor.ts also fails: editor.ts:1684-1702 uses the identical getBlockIndex + getContextBlocks() pairing, so the two walkers agree. The described header/footer mis-mutation is therefore not reachable as stated.
